To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) model checking is feasible on hierarchical systems; (2) the verification of linear-time temporal logic is polynomial-time; and (3) the verification of branching-time temporal logic is coNP-complete.
(1) model checking of hierarchical statecharts (HSCs) is decidable, and (2) it is possible to verify linear and branching time requirements on HSCs in polynomial time.
1) The model checking of hierarchical machines can be done in polynomial time.
In summary, our research is concerned with
model checking of nested state machines, a class of systems that are widely used in software engineering.
the development of efficient model checking techniques for hierarchical machines.
the development of model checking methods for the verification of hierarchical state machines, which are applicable in practice.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
hierarchical model checking is possible in a practical way, and is not much more expensive than ordinary model checking of non-hierarchical systems.
the model checking of nested systems can be done efficiently, in contrast to the exponential complexity of the flattening method.
the complexity of model checking is not affected by the hierarchical nature of the machine, as long as the requirements are linear time.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the complexity of model checking of hierarchical machines is the same as the one for checking flat machines.
we show that the model checking problem of hierarchical state machines is not harder than the model checking of ordinary state machines.
model checking of hierarchical state-machines is as easy as model checking of ordinary FSMs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
hierarchical state machines can be verified in a way that is both efficient and natural to the modeler.
the model checking problem for hierarchical machines can be solved more efficiently than for ordinary machines, even when the latter are obtained by flattening the former.
hierarchical state machines are amenable to model checking.
